description: Approval Rule entity: a firewall-style statement that maps an opportunity pattern and a resource selector to an action (PRD cpt-cf-approval-service-fr-approval-rules). Rules come from three layers (PRD cpt-cf-approval-service-fr-rule-layers): 'runtime' rules stored by the service (any tenant), 'configuration' rules from the approval service configuration file (root tenant only, read-only through the API), and 'gear_default' rules derived from each opportunity's default_action trait (root tenant only, read-only). Layers are read at verification time and never copied into one another. This type is the subject type of rule change events (DESIGN cpt-cf-approval-service-entity-rule).

id.description: Rule identifier. UUID for runtime rules; a stable synthetic identifier for configuration and gear-default rules.

layer.description: Rule layer. Enum evolution: closed by the PRD; a new layer requires a new major.

scope_tenant_id.description: Tenant the rule applies to, together with its descendants.

opportunity_pattern.description: GTS type identifier or wildcard pattern over opportunity types, with GTS wildcard and version-matching semantics, for example gts.cf.core.approval.opportunity.v1~cf.procurement.*.

subject_type_pattern.description: Optional subject type pattern (p2, PRD cpt-cf-approval-service-fr-subject-type-selector). Compared after the resource selector and the opportunity pattern for specificity.

action.description: Rule action. Strictness order: deny, require_approval, not_required. Enum evolution: closed by the PRD; a new action requires a new major.

overridable.description: Whether descendant runtime rules may relax this rule (p3, PRD cpt-cf-approval-service-fr-delegable-rules). Always false before p3.

reason.description: Reason recorded with the last change. Mandatory for runtime rules.

row_version.description: Optimistic concurrency version; exposed as the ETag of the rule.

ResourceSelector.description: Exactly one of: a projection type pattern, or one specific projection. A specific projection is more specific than any type pattern.
